struct lua_Callbacks
{
    void* userdata; // arbitrary userdata pointer that is never overwritten by Luau

    void (*interrupt)(lua_State* L, int gc);  // gets called at safepoints (loop back edges, call/ret, gc) if set
    void (*panic)(lua_State* L, int errcode); // gets called when an unprotected error is raised (if longjmp is used)

    void (*userthread)(lua_State* LP, lua_State* L); // gets called when L is created (LP == parent) or destroyed (LP == NULL)
    int16_t (*useratom)(const char* s, size_t l);    // gets called when a string is created; returned atom can be retrieved via tostringatom

    void (*debugbreak)(lua_State* L, lua_Debug* ar);     // gets called when BREAK instruction is encountered
    void (*debugstep)(lua_State* L, lua_Debug* ar);      // gets called after each instruction in single step mode
    void (*debuginterrupt)(lua_State* L, lua_Debug* ar); // gets called when thread execution is interrupted by break in another thread
    void (*debugprotectederror)(lua_State* L);           // gets called when protected call results in an error

    void (*onallocate)(lua_State* L, size_t osize, size_t nsize); // gets called when memory is allocated
};
typedef struct lua_Callbacks lua_Callbacks;

objects.description: Enumeration of builtin function identifiers used by FASTCALL opcodes to target VM-native implementations. Values are serialized; order is significant.

functions.name: lua_newstate
functions.signature: LUA_API lua_State* lua_newstate(lua_Alloc f, void* ud);
functions.description: Creates a new Luau VM state using the provided allocator and userdata. Returns a pointer to the newly created lua_State, or NULL on failure.
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer implementing lua_Alloc semantics (realloc-style: ptr/osize -> nsize).
ud is an opaque pointer passed to the allocator; can be NULL.
Callers must close the state with lua_close when no longer needed.
Not thread-safe to mutate callbacks except where noted in header comments.

functions.name: lua_close
functions.description: Destroys and frees a lua_State and all associated resources. After this call, L is invalid.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State returned by lua_newstate.
Must not be called concurrently with running code in L or its coroutines.
Do not use L after this call.

functions.name: lua_newthread
functions.description: Creates a new coroutine (thread) associated with the same global state as L and pushes it on L's stack. Returns the new thread state.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State.
Sufficient stack space on L to receive the new thread (use lua_checkstack if needed).

functions.name: lua_mainthread
functions.description: Returns the main thread (root coroutine) associated with the same global state as L.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State.

functions.name: lua_resetthread
functions.description: Resets a thread to its initial state, clearing its stack and coroutine status. Intended to reuse a coroutine.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State representing a thread.
Thread must not be running while being reset.

functions.name: lua_isthreadreset
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given thread has been reset and is in the reset state; zero otherwise.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State representing a thread.

functions.name: lua_absindex
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_absindex(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Converts a stack index, which may be relative or a pseudo-index, to an absolute index.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx can be any stack index or pseudo-index.

functions.name: lua_gettop
functions.description: Returns the index of the top element in the stack (number of elements).
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_settop
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_settop(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Sets the stack top to the given index. Shrinks or grows the stack; when growing, fills new slots with nil.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx can be positive, zero, or negative relative to current top; must not exceed stack capacity.
Ensure there is enough stack capacity or call lua_checkstack.

functions.name: lua_pushvalue
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushvalue(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Pushes a copy of the element at the given valid index onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid stack index or pseudo-index.
Stack must have room for one value; use lua_checkstack if needed.

functions.name: lua_remove
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_remove(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Removes the element at the given valid index, shifting down elements above it.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must refer to an existing stack element (not a pseudo-index).

functions.name: lua_insert
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_insert(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Moves the top element into the position given by idx, shifting up elements as needed.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid stack index (not pseudo-index).
Stack must be non-empty.

functions.name: lua_replace
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_replace(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Replaces the value at the given index with the top value and pops the top.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid stack index or pseudo-index.
Stack must be non-empty.

functions.name: lua_checkstack
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_checkstack(lua_State* L, int sz);
functions.description: Ensures that the stack has at least sz free slots. Returns non-zero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: L must be valid.
sz must be non-negative.

functions.name: lua_rawcheckstack
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_rawcheckstack(lua_State* L, int sz);
functions.description: Ensures the stack has at least sz free slots, allowing for unlimited stack frames (internal/unsafe variant).
requirements: L must be valid.
sz must be non-negative.
Caller must ensure this is safe in their embedding; bypasses some checks.

functions.name: lua_xmove
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_xmove(lua_State* from, lua_State* to, int n);
functions.description: Moves n values from the top of 'from' stack to the top of 'to' stack. Both threads must share the same global state.
requirements: from and to must be valid lua_State and belong to the same VM.
n must be between 0 and the number of elements on 'from' stack.
'to' must have enough free stack space.

functions.name: lua_xpush
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_xpush(lua_State* from, lua_State* to, int idx);
functions.description: Pushes onto 'to' a copy of the value at index idx from 'from'. Threads must share the same global state.
requirements: from and to must be valid and belong to the same VM.
idx must be a valid index in 'from'.
'to' must have enough free stack space.

functions.name: lua_isnumber
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_isnumber(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value at idx is a number (or convertible to number).
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_isstring
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_isstring(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value at idx is a string or number (typical Lua semantics).
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_iscfunction
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_iscfunction(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value at idx is a C function.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_isLfunction
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_isLfunction(lua_State* L, int idx);

idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_type

functions.name: lua_typename

tp should be a valid lua_Type value.

functions.name: lua_equal

functions.name: lua_rawequal

idx1 and idx2 must be valid indices.

functions.name: lua_lessthan
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_lessthan(lua_State* L, int idx1, int idx2);
functions.description: Performs less-than comparison between values at idx1 and idx2 according to Lua semantics. Returns non-zero if true.

idx1 and idx2 must be valid indices.
Values must be comparable under Lua rules; otherwise may raise an error.

functions.name: lua_tonumberx
functions.signature: LUA_API double lua_tonumberx(lua_State* L, int idx, int* isnum);
functions.description: Converts the value at idx to a number if possible. Returns the number or 0.0 on failure; if isnum is non-NULL, sets *isnum to 1 on success, 0 on failure.

isnum may be NULL or a valid pointer to int.

requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
isnum may be NULL or a valid pointer to int.

functions.name: lua_tounsignedx
functions.signature: LUA_API unsigned lua_tounsignedx(lua_State* L, int idx, int* isnum);
functions.description: Converts the value at idx to an unsigned integer if possible. Returns the value or 0 on failure; if isnum is non-NULL, sets *isnum accordingly.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
isnum may be NULL or a valid pointer to int.

functions.name: lua_tovector
functions.signature: LUA_API const float* lua_tovector(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a 3- or 4-component float vector at idx, or NULL if not a vector.

idx must be a valid index.
Returned pointer remains valid while the value remains on the stack and unmodified.

functions.name: lua_toboolean
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_toboolean(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Converts the value at idx to a boolean (Lua truthiness). Returns 0 or 1.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_tolstring
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_tolstring(lua_State* L, int idx, size_t* len);
functions.description: Converts the value at idx to a string (if needed) and returns a pointer to the internal string plus its length via len if non-NULL.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
len may be NULL or a valid pointer.
Returned pointer is valid while the value remains on the stack and unmodified.

functions.name: lua_tostringatom
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_tostringatom(lua_State* L, int idx, int* atom);
functions.description: Returns the string representation of the value at idx and stores its atom ID via 'atom' if provided.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
atom may be NULL or a valid pointer to int.
Returned pointer lifetime matches lua_tolstring semantics.

functions.name: lua_tolstringatom
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_tolstringatom(lua_State* L, int idx, size_t* len, int* atom);
functions.description: Converts value at idx to string and returns pointer, length via len, and atom ID via atom.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
len and atom may be NULL or valid pointers.
Returned pointer lifetime matches lua_tolstring semantics.

functions.name: lua_namecallatom
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_namecallatom(lua_State* L, int* atom);
functions.description: Returns the name used in the most recent namecall context and its atom ID via atom.
requirements: L must be valid.
atom may be NULL or a valid pointer to int.
Only meaningful when called within a namecall context.

functions.name: lua_objlen
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_objlen(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns the length of the object at idx using length semantics (string length, table length, etc.).
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_tocfunction
functions.signature: LUA_API lua_CFunction lua_tocfunction(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: If the value at idx is a C function, returns its C function pointer; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_tolightuserdata
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_tolightuserdata(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns the light userdata pointer at idx or NULL if not light userdata.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_tolightuserdatatagged
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_tolightuserdatatagged(lua_State* L, int idx, int tag);
functions.description: Returns the light userdata pointer at idx if it carries the specified tag; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_touserdata
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_touserdata(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to block of full userdata at idx or NULL if not userdata.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_touserdatatagged
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_touserdatatagged(lua_State* L, int idx, int tag);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to full userdata at idx if it has the specified tag; otherwise NULL.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_userdatatag
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_userdatatag(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns the tag associated with the full userdata at idx, or 0/unknown if not applicable.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index containing full userdata.

functions.name: lua_lightuserdatatag
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_lightuserdatatag(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns the tag associated with the light userdata at idx, or 0/unknown if not applicable.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index containing light userdata.

functions.name: lua_tothread
functions.signature: LUA_API lua_State* lua_tothread(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns the thread (lua_State*) stored at idx, or NULL if not a thread.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_tobuffer
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_tobuffer(lua_State* L, int idx, size_t* len);
functions.description: If value at idx is a buffer, returns its data pointer and writes its size to len if non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
len may be NULL or a valid pointer.
Returned pointer valid while buffer value is alive and unmodified.

functions.name: lua_topointer
functions.signature: LUA_API const void* lua_topointer(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns an address that identifies the Lua value at idx (pointer identity) or NULL if not applicable.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
Not a stable pointer to object contents; for identity only.

functions.name: lua_pushnil
functions.description: Pushes nil onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushnumber
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushnumber(lua_State* L, double n);
functions.description: Pushes a number onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushinteger
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushinteger(lua_State* L, int n);
functions.description: Pushes an integer onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushunsigned
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushunsigned(lua_State* L, unsigned n);
functions.description: Pushes an unsigned integer onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushvector
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushvector(lua_State* L, float x, float y, float z, float w);
functions.description: Pushes a 4D vector value onto the stack. Signature is active when LUA_VECTOR_SIZE == 4.
requirements: L must be valid.
Ensure stack has space for one value.
Only available when LUA_VECTOR_SIZE==4 at compile time.

functions.name: lua_pushlstring
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushlstring(lua_State* L, const char* s, size_t l);
functions.description: Pushes a string of length l from buffer s onto the stack; allows embedded nulls.
requirements: L must be valid.
s must point to at least l bytes; can be NULL only if l==0.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushstring
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushstring(lua_State* L, const char* s);
functions.description: Pushes a null-terminated C string onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
s must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated string (or NULL to push nil in some Lua variants; behavior here assumed to create empty string or nil is unknown).
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushvfstring
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_pushvfstring(lua_State* L, const char* fmt, va_list argp);
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-like fmt and va_list, pushes it, and returns the internal pointer.
requirements: L must be valid.
fmt must be a valid format string.
argp must be a valid va_list.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushfstringL
functions.signature: LUA_API LUA_PRINTF_ATTR(2, 3) const char* lua_pushfstringL(lua_State* L, const char* fmt, ...);
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-like fmt and varargs, pushes it, and returns the internal pointer.
requirements: L must be valid.
fmt must be a valid format string; arguments must match specifiers.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushcclosurek
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushcclosurek(lua_State* L, lua_CFunction fn, const char* debugname, int nup, lua_Continuation cont);
functions.description: Pushes a C function with nup upvalues as a closure; optionally sets a continuation for yields and a debug name.
requirements: L must be valid.
fn must be a valid C function pointer.
debugname may be NULL or a valid string.
nup must be >= 0 and that many values must be on the stack as upvalues.
cont may be NULL or a valid continuation function.

functions.name: lua_pushboolean
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushboolean(lua_State* L, int b);
functions.description: Pushes a boolean value onto the stack (0=false, non-zero=true).
requirements: L must be valid.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushthread
functions.description: Pushes the current thread onto the stack. Returns 1 if this is the main thread, 0 otherwise.
requirements: L must be valid.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_pushlightuserdatatagged
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_pushlightuserdatatagged(lua_State* L, void* p, int tag);
functions.description: Pushes a light userdata pointer with an associated integer tag onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
p may be any pointer (including NULL if allowed).
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_newuserdatatagged
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_newuserdatatagged(lua_State* L, size_t sz, int tag);
functions.description: Allocates a new full userdata block of size sz with a tag and pushes it on the stack. Returns the data pointer.
requirements: L must be valid.
sz must be >= 0; large sizes may fail due to memory.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_newuserdatataggedwithmetatable
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_newuserdatataggedwithmetatable(lua_State* L, size_t sz, int tag);
functions.description: Like lua_newuserdatatagged but assigns a metatable previously registered for the given tag via lua_setuserdatametatable.
requirements: L must be valid.
sz must be >= 0.
Associated metatable for 'tag' must have been set via lua_setuserdatametatable.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_newuserdatadtor
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_newuserdatadtor(lua_State* L, size_t sz, void (*dtor)(void*));
functions.description: Allocates a new full userdata block of size sz with a custom destructor to be called when the userdata is collected.
requirements: L must be valid.
sz must be >= 0.
dtor may be NULL or a valid function pointer; if non-NULL it must be safe to call at GC time.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_newbuffer
functions.signature: LUA_API void* lua_newbuffer(lua_State* L, size_t sz);
functions.description: Allocates and pushes a new mutable buffer object of size sz; returns its data pointer.
requirements: L must be valid.
sz must be >= 0.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_gettable
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_gettable(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Pushes t[k] where t is the value at idx and k is on the top of the stack; pops the key and pushes the result. Returns the type of the pushed value.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table or value with __index metamethod.
Top of stack must contain key.
May invoke metamethods and raise errors.

functions.name: lua_getfield
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_getfield(lua_State* L, int idx, const char* k);
functions.description: Pushes t[k] for string key k; returns the type of the pushed value.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table or value with __index metamethod.
k must be a valid C string pointer.

functions.name: lua_rawgetfield
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_rawgetfield(lua_State* L, int idx, const char* k);
functions.description: Pushes raw t[k] for string key k without invoking metamethods; returns the type of the pushed value.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
k must be a valid C string pointer.

functions.name: lua_rawget
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_rawget(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Pushes raw t[k] where key k is on the top of the stack; no metamethods. Returns the type of the pushed value.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
Top of stack must contain key.

functions.name: lua_rawgeti
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_rawgeti(lua_State* L, int idx, int n);
functions.description: Pushes raw t[n] (integer key) from table at idx; returns the type of the pushed value.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.

functions.name: lua_rawgetptagged
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_rawgetptagged(lua_State* L, int idx, void* p, int tag);
functions.description: Pushes raw t[p] for pointer key p with tag filter; returns the type of the pushed value.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.

functions.name: lua_createtable
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_createtable(lua_State* L, int narr, int nrec);
functions.description: Creates a new table with array part preallocated for narr elements and hash part for nrec elements, and pushes it.
requirements: L must be valid.
narr and nrec must be >= 0.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_setreadonly
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setreadonly(lua_State* L, int idx, int enabled);
functions.description: Marks the table or userdata at idx as read-only or read-write.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table or userdata.
enabled must be 0 or non-zero.

functions.name: lua_getreadonly
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_getreadonly(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the object at idx is read-only; zero otherwise.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table or userdata.

functions.name: lua_setsafeenv
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setsafeenv(lua_State* L, int idx, int enabled);
functions.description: Marks the function or thread at idx as having a safe environment (restricts access).
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a function or thread.
enabled must be 0 or non-zero.

functions.name: lua_getmetatable
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_getmetatable(lua_State* L, int objindex);
functions.description: Pushes the metatable of the value at objindex if it exists; returns 1 if metatable pushed, 0 otherwise.
requirements: L must be valid.
objindex must be a valid index.

functions.name: lua_getfenv
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_getfenv(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Pushes the environment table of the value at idx (function/thread).
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a function or thread.

functions.name: lua_settable
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_settable(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Performs t[k]=v where t is at idx and key and value are on top of the stack (value at top, key below); pops both.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table or object with __newindex metamethod.
Top two stack values must be present: value, key.
May invoke metamethods and raise errors.

functions.name: lua_setfield
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setfield(lua_State* L, int idx, const char* k);
functions.description: Sets t[k]=v for string key k, where v is on top of the stack; pops v.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table or object with __newindex.
k must be a valid C string pointer.
Top of stack must contain value.

functions.name: lua_rawsetfield
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_rawsetfield(lua_State* L, int idx, const char* k);
functions.description: Performs raw set t[k]=v for string key k without metamethods; pops v.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
k must be a valid C string pointer.
Top of stack must contain value.

functions.name: lua_rawset
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_rawset(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Performs raw set t[k]=v with key and value on top of the stack; pops both.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
Top two stack values must be present: value, key.

functions.name: lua_rawseti
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_rawseti(lua_State* L, int idx, int n);
functions.description: Performs raw set t[n]=v for integer key n; pops v.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
Top of stack must contain value.

functions.name: lua_rawsetptagged
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_rawsetptagged(lua_State* L, int idx, void* p, int tag);
functions.description: Performs raw set t[p]=v for pointer key p with tag filter; pops v.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
Top of stack must contain value.

functions.name: lua_setmetatable
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_setmetatable(lua_State* L, int objindex);
functions.description: Sets the metatable for the value at objindex to the table at the top of the stack (or nil to clear). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: L must be valid.
objindex must be a valid index to a table/userdata.
Top of stack must contain a table or nil; will be popped.

functions.name: lua_setfenv
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_setfenv(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Sets the environment table for the value at idx to the table at the top of the stack; returns non-zero on success.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a function or thread.
Top of stack must contain a table; will be popped.

functions.name: luau_load
functions.signature: LUA_API int luau_load(lua_State* L, const char* chunkname, const char* data, size_t size, int env);
functions.description: Loads Luau bytecode from buffer 'data' of size 'size' as chunk named 'chunkname' and sets its environment (env index). Pushes the compiled function on success. Returns a status code from lua_Status.
requirements: L must be valid.
data must point to 'size' bytes of valid Luau bytecode.
chunkname may be NULL or a valid C string.
env is a stack index or special value designating environment.
On error, leaves error object on stack and returns LUA_ERR*.

functions.name: lua_call
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_call(lua_State* L, int nargs, int nresults);
functions.description: Calls a function. The function and its 'nargs' arguments must be on the stack. On return, results replace the function and arguments.
requirements: L must be valid.
Stack must contain function followed by nargs arguments.
nresults is number of expected results or LUA_MULTRET.
Errors are not protected; they longjmp/panic unless caught externally.

functions.name: lua_pcall
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_pcall(lua_State* L, int nargs, int nresults, int errfunc);

requirements: L must be valid.
Stack must contain function followed by nargs arguments.
nresults is number of expected results or LUA_MULTRET.
errfunc is 0 or a valid stack index to an error handler function.

functions.name: lua_cpcall
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_cpcall(lua_State* L, lua_CFunction func, void* ud);
functions.description: Protected call to a C function 'func' with userdata 'ud'. Returns LUA_OK or an error code on failure.
requirements: L must be valid.
func must be a valid C function pointer.

functions.name: lua_yield
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_yield(lua_State* L, int nresults);
functions.description: Yields execution of the current coroutine, returning nresults values to the resumer. Returns a status code to the resumer.
requirements: L must be a yieldable coroutine (see lua_isyieldable).
nresults must match number of values on top to return.

functions.name: lua_break
functions.description: Yields the current thread for a debug breakpoint. Returns LUA_BREAK status.
requirements: L must be valid.
Intended for debug hook usage.

functions.name: lua_resume
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_resume(lua_State* L, lua_State* from, int narg);
functions.description: Resumes a suspended coroutine L from thread 'from' passing narg values. Returns a status code (LUA_OK, LUA_YIELD, LUA_COERR, etc.).
requirements: L and from must be valid and belong to the same VM.
L must be in a resumable state (suspended).
Stack of L must have space for arguments; 'from' must push them appropriately.

functions.name: lua_resumeerror
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_resumeerror(lua_State* L, lua_State* from);
functions.description: Resumes a coroutine L propagating a previously stored error. Used to continue error handling paths. Returns status code.
requirements: L and from must be valid and belong to the same VM.
L must be in a state expecting an error resume.

functions.name: lua_status
functions.description: Returns the thread status (lua_Status) of L.
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_isyieldable
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the current thread is yieldable; zero otherwise.
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_getthreaddata
functions.description: Returns the user data pointer associated with the thread L.
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_setthreaddata
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setthreaddata(lua_State* L, void* data);
functions.description: Sets an arbitrary user data pointer for the thread L.
requirements: L must be valid.
data can be NULL or any pointer.

functions.name: lua_costatus
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_costatus(lua_State* L, lua_State* co);
functions.description: Returns the coroutine status (lua_CoStatus) of coroutine 'co' from the perspective of thread L.
requirements: L and co must be valid and belong to the same VM.

functions.name: lua_gc
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_gc(lua_State* L, int what, int data);
functions.description: Controls garbage collection with operation 'what' (lua_GCOp) and argument 'data'. Returns operation-dependent result (e.g., counts).
requirements: L must be valid.
what must be one of lua_GCOp values.
'data' meaning depends on 'what' (e.g., KB for LUA_GCSTEP).

functions.name: lua_setmemcat
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setmemcat(lua_State* L, int category);
functions.description: Sets the current memory category for allocations attributed to running thread (0..LUA_MEMORY_CATEGORIES-1).
requirements: L must be valid.
category must be within 0..LUA_MEMORY_CATEGORIES-1.

functions.name: lua_totalbytes
functions.signature: LUA_API size_t lua_totalbytes(lua_State* L, int category);
functions.description: Returns the total bytes allocated for the given memory category in the current VM.
requirements: L must be valid.
category must be valid (0..LUA_MEMORY_CATEGORIES-1).

functions.name: lua_error
functions.description: Raises a Lua error with the object on top of the stack and does not return (longjmp/exception).
requirements: L must be valid.
Top of stack must contain an error object/message.
Control will not return; embedder must be prepared for non-local exit.

functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_next(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Iterates over table at idx. On entry, key is on top (or nil to start). Pops key and pushes next key-value pair; returns 1 while elements remain, 0 when done.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
Key management must follow Lua's iteration protocol.

functions.name: lua_rawiter
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_rawiter(lua_State* L, int idx, int iter);
functions.description: Performs raw iteration over table at idx using internal iterator state 'iter'; returns non-zero while elements remain.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
'iter' is an opaque iteration cursor value obtained from previous calls.

functions.name: lua_concat
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_concat(lua_State* L, int n);
functions.description: Concatenates the top n values on the stack into a single string and pushes the result.
requirements: L must be valid.
n must be >= 0 and not exceed the number of stack values.
Values must be concatenable (strings/numbers or metamethods).

functions.name: lua_encodepointer
functions.signature: LUA_API uintptr_t lua_encodepointer(lua_State* L, uintptr_t p);
functions.description: Encodes a pointer value for safe use as a table key or identity token; returns encoded value.
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_clock
functions.description: Returns a monotonic or process CPU clock time as a double. Exact semantics depend on implementation.

functions.name: lua_setuserdatatag
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setuserdatatag(lua_State* L, int idx, int tag);
functions.description: Sets the tag associated with the userdata value at idx.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference full userdata.
Tag is an integer; semantics defined by the embedder.

functions.name: lua_setuserdatadtor
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setuserdatadtor(lua_State* L, int tag, lua_Destructor dtor);
functions.description: Registers a destructor callback for userdata with the given tag. Called on collection with (L, userdata).
requirements: L must be valid.
dtor may be NULL or a valid function pointer. Callback must be safe during GC.

functions.name: lua_getuserdatadtor
functions.signature: LUA_API lua_Destructor lua_getuserdatadtor(lua_State* L, int tag);
functions.description: Retrieves the registered destructor for userdata tag, or NULL if none.
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_setuserdatametatable
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setuserdatametatable(lua_State* L, int tag);
functions.description: Associates the metatable currently on top of the stack with the given userdata tag for later use. Intended to pair with lua_newuserdatataggedwithmetatable.
requirements: L must be valid.
Top of stack must be a metatable (table) to associate; will be consumed per implementation semantics.

functions.name: lua_getuserdatametatable
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_getuserdatametatable(lua_State* L, int tag);
functions.description: Pushes the metatable registered for the given userdata tag onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
A metatable must have been registered for this tag.

functions.name: lua_setlightuserdataname
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_setlightuserdataname(lua_State* L, int tag, const char* name);
functions.description: Associates a human-readable name with a light userdata tag for debugging.
requirements: L must be valid.
name must be a valid C string pointer or NULL.

functions.name: lua_getlightuserdataname
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_getlightuserdataname(lua_State* L, int tag);
functions.description: Retrieves the name associated with a light userdata tag, or NULL if none.
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_clonefunction
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_clonefunction(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Clones the function at idx (duplicating its prototype/closures) and pushes the clone onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a function value.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_cleartable
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_cleartable(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Removes all entries from the table at idx, leaving it empty.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.

functions.name: lua_clonetable
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_clonetable(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Creates a shallow clone of the table at idx and pushes the new table onto the stack.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must reference a table.
Ensure stack has space for one value.

functions.name: lua_getallocf
functions.signature: LUA_API lua_Alloc lua_getallocf(lua_State* L, void** ud);
functions.description: Returns the allocator function used by the VM and stores its 'ud' userdata in *ud if non-NULL.
requirements: L must be valid.
ud may be NULL or a valid pointer to void*.

functions.name: lua_ref
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_ref(lua_State* L, int idx);
functions.description: Creates a strong reference in the registry for the value at idx and returns an integer reference ID.
requirements: L must be valid.
idx must be a valid index.
Reference must be released with lua_unref to avoid leaks.

functions.name: lua_unref
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_unref(lua_State* L, int ref);
functions.description: Releases a reference previously created by lua_ref. After this, 'ref' becomes invalid.
requirements: L must be valid.
ref must be a reference returned by lua_ref, or LUA_NOREF/LUA_REFNIL.

functions.name: lua_stackdepth
functions.description: Returns the current call stack depth for thread L.
requirements: L must be valid.

functions.name: lua_getinfo
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_getinfo(lua_State* L, int level, const char* what, lua_Debug* ar);
functions.description: Fills a lua_Debug record with information about the function/activation at 'level', controlled by the 'what' string. Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: L must be valid.
what must be a valid option string specifying requested fields.
ar must be a valid pointer to lua_Debug.

functions.name: lua_getargument
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_getargument(lua_State* L, int level, int n);
functions.description: Pushes the nth argument of the function at call stack level 'level' onto the stack. Returns the argument type.
requirements: L must be valid.
'level' must be a valid stack frame.
'n' must refer to an existing argument index.

functions.name: lua_getlocal
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_getlocal(lua_State* L, int level, int n);
functions.description: Pushes the value of the nth local variable at call stack level 'level' and returns its name, or NULL if not available.
requirements: L must be valid.
'level' must be a valid stack frame.
'n' selects a local variable index in that frame.

functions.name: lua_setlocal
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_setlocal(lua_State* L, int level, int n);
functions.description: Sets the nth local variable at call stack level 'level' to the value on top of the stack and returns its name, or NULL if not available.
requirements: L must be valid.
'level' must be a valid stack frame.
Top of stack must contain the new value.
'n' selects a local variable index.

functions.name: lua_getupvalue
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_getupvalue(lua_State* L, int funcindex, int n);
functions.description: Pushes the value of the nth upvalue of the function at funcindex and returns its name, or NULL if not available.
requirements: L must be valid.
funcindex must reference a function.
n must be >= 1 and within upvalue count.

functions.name: lua_setupvalue
functions.signature: LUA_API const char* lua_setupvalue(lua_State* L, int funcindex, int n);
functions.description: Sets the nth upvalue of the function at funcindex to the value on top of the stack and returns its name, or NULL if not available.
requirements: L must be valid.
funcindex must reference a function.
n must be >= 1 and within upvalue count.
Top of stack must contain the new value.

functions.name: lua_singlestep
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_singlestep(lua_State* L, int enabled);
functions.description: Enables or disables single-step debug mode for thread L. When enabled, debugstep callback is invoked after each instruction.
requirements: L must be valid.
enabled must be 0 or non-zero.

functions.name: lua_breakpoint
functions.signature: LUA_API int lua_breakpoint(lua_State* L, int funcindex, int line, int enabled);
functions.description: Enables or disables a breakpoint at a location (function and line). Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: L must be valid.
funcindex must reference a function.
line must be a valid line number in function, if applicable.
enabled must be 0 or non-zero.

functions.name: lua_getcoverage
functions.signature: LUA_API void lua_getcoverage(lua_State* L, int funcindex, void* context, lua_Coverage callback);
functions.description: Invokes 'callback' with coverage data for the function at funcindex. Callback receives function name, defined line, depth, hit counts array, and size.
requirements: L must be valid.
funcindex must reference a function.
callback must be a valid function pointer; may be called multiple times.
context is passed through to callback; may be NULL.

functions.name: lua_debugtrace
functions.description: Returns a human-readable stack trace string for debugging. Not thread-safe; uses a shared static buffer.
requirements: L must be valid.
Result is stored in a shared global buffer; must not be used concurrently by multiple threads.

functions.name: lua_callbacks
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the VM-wide callbacks structure that can be modified to adjust VM behavior (interrupt, panic, hooks, allocation).
requirements: L must be valid.
Except for 'interrupt', callbacks must be changed only when the VM is not running any code (per header note).
Returned pointer remains valid while VM exists.

functions.name: luaL_register
functions.signature: void luaL_register(lua_State* L, const char* libname, const luaL_Reg* l)
functions.description: Registers a list of C functions (array of luaL_Reg) into a Lua table. If libname is non-null, creates/gets a table with that name and registers functions into it; if null, registers into the current table on the stack. Typical use is to expose a C library to Lua.
requirements: L must be a valid, initialized lua_State*.
l must point to a null-terminated array of luaL_Reg entries (last entry has name==NULL).
If libname is NULL, a table must be present at the top of the stack to receive the functions.
Each luaL_Reg.func must be a valid lua_CFunction.

functions.name: luaL_getmetafield
functions.signature: int luaL_getmetafield(lua_State* L, int obj, const char* e)
functions.description: Pushes the value of field e from the metatable of the value at stack index obj, if it exists. Returns nonzero if the metafield was found and pushed, zero otherwise.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
obj must be a valid stack index referring to a value.
e must be a non-null C string naming the metafield.

functions.name: luaL_callmeta
functions.signature: int luaL_callmeta(lua_State* L, int obj, const char* e)
functions.description: Calls the metafield e of the value at index obj (if present) as a function, passing the object as the first argument. Returns nonzero if the call was performed, zero otherwise.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
obj must be a valid stack index referring to a value.
e must be a non-null C string naming the metafield.
If the metafield exists, it must be callable; otherwise an error may be raised during call.

functions.name: luaL_typeerrorL
functions.signature: l_noret luaL_typeerrorL(lua_State* L, int narg, const char* tname)
functions.description: Raises a type error for argument narg, indicating the expected type name tname. This function does not return.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
tname should be a non-null, human-readable expected type description.
Control flow does not return; callers should not expect a return value.

functions.name: luaL_argerrorL
functions.signature: l_noret luaL_argerrorL(lua_State* L, int narg, const char* extramsg)
functions.description: Raises an argument error for argument narg with an additional message extramsg. This function does not return.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
extramsg should be a non-null C string with additional error details.
Control flow does not return; callers should not expect a return value.

functions.name: luaL_checklstring
functions.signature: const char* luaL_checklstring(lua_State* L, int numArg, size_t* l)
functions.description: Checks that the function argument at index numArg is a string and returns a pointer to its internal buffer; if l is non-null, stores its length in *l. Raises an error if the value is not a string/coercible string.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
numArg must be a valid stack index referring to a value.
If l is non-null, it must be a valid pointer to size_t for output.
Caller must not modify the returned string data.

functions.name: luaL_optlstring
functions.signature: const char* luaL_optlstring(lua_State* L, int numArg, const char* def, size_t* l)
functions.description: Returns the string at index numArg, like luaL_checklstring, or def if the argument is absent or nil. If l is non-null, stores string length in *l. Raises an error if present but not a string/coercible string.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
If the argument is present and not nil, it must be a string/coercible string.
If l is non-null, it must be a valid pointer to size_t for output.
def may be NULL; if used, length reported in *l (if non-null) corresponds to def.

functions.name: luaL_checknumber
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index numArg is a number and returns it as a C double. Raises an error if not a number/coercible to number.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
numArg must be a valid stack index referring to a value that is a number or coercible to a number.

functions.name: luaL_optnumber
functions.signature: double luaL_optnumber(lua_State* L, int nArg, double def)
functions.description: Returns the numeric value at index nArg as a C double, or def if the argument is absent or nil. Raises an error if present but not a number/coercible to number.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
If the argument at nArg is present and not nil, it must be a number or coercible to a number.

functions.name: luaL_checkboolean
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index narg is a boolean and returns it as an int (0 or 1). Raises an error if not a boolean.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
narg must refer to a boolean value on the stack.

functions.name: luaL_optboolean
functions.signature: int luaL_optboolean(lua_State* L, int narg, int def)
functions.description: Returns the boolean value at index narg as int (0 or 1), or def if the argument is absent or nil. Raises an error if present but not a boolean.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
If the argument at narg is present and not nil, it must be a boolean value.

functions.name: luaL_checkinteger
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index numArg is an integer and returns it as int. Raises an error if not an integer/coercible integer.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
numArg must refer to an integer value or a value coercible to integer within the C int range.

functions.name: luaL_optinteger
functions.signature: int luaL_optinteger(lua_State* L, int nArg, int def)
functions.description: Returns the integer value at index nArg as int, or def if the argument is absent or nil. Raises an error if present but not an integer/coercible integer.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
If the argument at nArg is present and not nil, it must be an integer or coercible to integer within the C int range.

functions.name: luaL_checkunsigned
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index numArg is an unsigned integer and returns it as unsigned. Raises an error if not an unsigned/coercible value.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
numArg must refer to a value that can be represented as an unsigned (non-negative) integer.

functions.name: luaL_optunsigned
functions.signature: unsigned luaL_optunsigned(lua_State* L, int numArg, unsigned def)
functions.description: Returns the unsigned integer value at index numArg, or def if the argument is absent or nil. Raises an error if present but not convertible to unsigned.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
If the argument at numArg is present and not nil, it must be representable as an unsigned integer.

functions.name: luaL_checkvector
functions.signature: const float* luaL_checkvector(lua_State* L, int narg)
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index narg is a vector value and returns a pointer to its float[3/4]-like storage (implementation-defined). Raises an error if the argument is not a vector.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
narg must refer to a vector value supported by Luau.
Returned pointer must be treated as read-only.

functions.name: luaL_optvector
functions.signature: const float* luaL_optvector(lua_State* L, int narg, const float* def)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the vector at index narg, or def if the argument is absent or nil. Raises an error if present but not a vector.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
If the argument at narg is present and not nil, it must be a vector value.
def may be NULL; callers must handle NULL when provided as default.

functions.name: luaL_checkstack
functions.signature: void luaL_checkstack(lua_State* L, int sz, const char* msg)
functions.description: Ensures that the stack has at least sz extra slots available; raises an error with msg if it cannot grow.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
sz must be a non-negative number of extra stack slots requested.
msg may be NULL; if non-null should describe the context.

functions.name: luaL_checktype
functions.signature: void luaL_checktype(lua_State* L, int narg, int t)
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index narg has Lua type t (e.g., LUA_TSTRING) and raises an error otherwise.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
narg must be a valid stack index.
t must be a valid Lua type tag constant.

functions.name: luaL_checkany
functions.description: Checks that there is any value (not absent) at stack index narg; raises an error if the argument is missing.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
narg must be a valid stack index for the current call frame.

functions.name: luaL_newmetatable
functions.signature: int luaL_newmetatable(lua_State* L, const char* tname)
functions.description: Creates a new metatable with name tname and pushes it onto the stack, or pushes the existing one if already created. Returns 1 if a new metatable was created, 0 if it already existed.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
tname must be a non-null unique registry name for the metatable.

functions.name: luaL_checkudata
functions.signature: void* luaL_checkudata(lua_State* L, int ud, const char* tname)
functions.description: Checks that the value at index ud is a userdata with metatable tname and returns its memory block pointer. Raises an error otherwise.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
ud must be a valid stack index referring to a userdata.
tname must match the metatable name with which the userdata was created.

functions.name: luaL_checkbuffer
functions.signature: void* luaL_checkbuffer(lua_State* L, int narg, size_t* len)
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index narg is a buffer-like object and returns a pointer to its data; writes its length to *len if non-null. Raises an error otherwise.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_state*.
narg must refer to a buffer value supported by Luau.
If len is non-null, it must be a valid pointer to size_t for output.
Returned pointer is valid according to the buffer object's lifetime; callers must not write unless the API guarantees mutability.

functions.name: luaL_where
functions.description: Pushes onto the stack a string describing the source location at call stack level lvl (e.g., file:line:). Useful for building error messages.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
lvl is a non-negative call stack level; values outside the call stack depth may yield generic location information.

functions.name: luaL_errorL
functions.signature: LUA_PRINTF_ATTR(2, 3) l_noret luaL_errorL(lua_State* L, const char* fmt, ...)
functions.description: Raises a formatted error with message produced by printf-like fmt and arguments. This function does not return. The attribute indicates printf-style format checking.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
fmt must be a non-null C format string compatible with the provided varargs.
Control flow does not return; callers should not expect a return value.

functions.name: luaL_checkoption
functions.signature: int luaL_checkoption(lua_State* L, int narg, const char* def, const char* const lst[])
functions.description: Checks that the argument at index narg is one of the strings in lst and returns its index in lst; if absent or nil, uses def. Raises an error if not found.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
lst must be a null-terminated array of const char* option names.
If the argument is present and not nil, it must be a string; otherwise def must be either a valid option string or NULL (error if not found).

functions.name: luaL_tolstring
functions.signature: const char* luaL_tolstring(lua_State* L, int idx, size_t* len)
functions.description: Converts the value at index idx to a string using the __tostring metamethod if available, pushes the result on the stack, and returns its pointer; if len is non-null, stores the string length. Returns pointer to the internal string representation.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
idx must be a valid stack index referring to a value.
If len is non-null, it must be a valid pointer to size_t for output.
Resulting string is pushed on the stack; caller must account for the extra stack slot.

functions.name: luaL_newstate
functions.description: Creates and returns a new Lua state. Typically used before opening libraries. Caller is responsible for closing the state when done.
requirements: Successful return yields a non-null lua_State*; on failure may return NULL (depending on implementation).
Caller should close the state using the appropriate API (e.g., lua_close) when finished.

functions.name: luaL_findtable
functions.signature: const char* luaL_findtable(lua_State* L, int idx, const char* fname, int szhint)
functions.description: Ensures that the table at index idx contains the nested table path specified by dot-separated fname, creating intermediate tables as needed up to size hint szhint. Returns NULL on success, or a string with the part of the name where a non-table value was found.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
idx must refer to a table on the stack.
fname may be NULL or a dot-separated path; if non-null, components must be valid strings.
szhint is a size hint for created tables; should be non-negative.

functions.name: luaL_typename
functions.signature: const char* luaL_typename(lua_State* L, int idx)
functions.description: Returns the type name of the value at stack index idx as a constant string.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
idx must be a valid stack index.

functions.name: luaL_callyieldable
functions.signature: int luaL_callyieldable(lua_State* L, int nargs, int nresults)
functions.description: Calls a Lua function in a way that is safe for yieldable C functions. The function and its nargs arguments must be on the stack. Returns status compatible with Lua call conventions.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
A callable value (function) must be below its nargs arguments on the stack before the call.
nargs must match the number of arguments pushed for the call.
nresults indicates the number of expected results, using Lua’s conventions (e.g., LUA_MULTRET).

functions.name: luaL_buffinit
functions.description: Initializes a string buffer B for efficient string building associated with state L. Must be called before any buffer operations on B.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
B must be a valid pointer to luaL_Strbuf storage.
B must not be used concurrently in multiple active builds without reinitialization.

functions.name: luaL_buffinitsize
functions.signature: char* luaL_buffinitsize(lua_State* L, luaL_Strbuf* B, size_t size)
functions.description: Initializes buffer B and ensures at least size bytes are available for writing. Returns a pointer to the writable area.
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
B must be a valid pointer to luaL_Strbuf storage.
size specifies the minimum writable space requested.

functions.name: luaL_prepbuffsize
functions.description: Ensures that buffer B has at least size bytes of free space and returns a pointer to the beginning of the free area. May push/prepare internal storage on the stack when growing.
requirements: B must be a valid, previously initialized buffer (via luaL_buffinit or luaL_buffinitsize).
size is the minimum number of free bytes requested and may be greater than current free space.
Callers must update B->p appropriately after writing data.

functions.name: luaL_addlstring
functions.signature: void luaL_addlstring(luaL_Strbuf* B, const char* s, size_t l)
functions.description: Appends l bytes from string s to buffer B, growing the buffer if necessary.
requirements: B must be initialized with luaL_buffinit/luaL_buffinitsize.
s must be a valid pointer to a buffer of at least l bytes (may contain binary data).
l may be zero; in that case, no data is appended.

functions.name: luaL_addvalue
functions.description: Appends the value on top of the stack to buffer B, popping it. Expects a string value at the top and the buffer’s mutable string below it as per Luau’s convention.
requirements: B must be initialized and associated with the current L.
The string value to append must be at the top of the stack.
The mutable string buffer value must be below the top (at top-2), per the header comment.
The value must be a string (or convertible as per implementation); errors may be raised otherwise.

functions.name: luaL_addvalueany
functions.description: Appends the value at stack index idx to buffer B, converting it to string as needed, and does not necessarily pop it unless specified by implementation. Useful for appending arbitrary values.
requirements: B must be initialized and associated with the current L.
idx must be a valid stack index referring to the value to append.
Value must be convertible to string per Lua’s tostring/__tostring semantics; errors may be raised otherwise.

functions.name: luaL_pushresult
functions.description: Finishes the buffer and pushes the resulting immutable string onto the stack. After this call, B is no longer valid for further appends until reinitialized.
requirements: B must be initialized and in a valid building state.
After pushing the result, callers should not continue writing to B without reinitializing.

functions.name: luaL_pushresultsize
functions.description: Like luaL_pushresult, but finalizes exactly size bytes from the buffer into the resulting string and pushes it on the stack.
requirements: B must be initialized and in a valid building state with at least size bytes of written data ready to finalize.
size must not exceed the number of bytes actually written into the buffer.

functions.name: luaopen_base
functions.description: Opens and registers the base library into the given Lua state, pushing the library table or return value(s) on the stack. Returns the number of results pushed (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
Should be called during library initialization or via require-like mechanisms.

functions.name: luaopen_coroutine
functions.description: Opens and registers the coroutine library into the given Lua state; pushes the library table and returns the number of results (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
Should be called during library initialization or via require-like mechanisms.

functions.name: luaopen_table
functions.description: Opens and registers the table library; pushes the library table and returns the number of results (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
Should be called during library initialization or via require-like mechanisms.

functions.name: luaopen_os
functions.description: Opens and registers the os library; pushes the library table and returns the number of results (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
May be restricted/modified by sandboxing policies.

functions.name: luaopen_string
functions.description: Opens and registers the string library; pushes the library table and returns the number of results (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
Should be called during library initialization or via require-like mechanisms.

functions.name: luaopen_bit32
functions.description: Opens and registers the bit32 library; pushes the library table and returns the number of results (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
Should be called during library initialization or via require-like mechanisms.

functions.name: luaopen_buffer
functions.description: Opens and registers the buffer library; pushes the library table and returns the number of results (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
Should be called during library initialization or via require-like mechanisms.

functions.name: luaopen_utf8
functions.description: Opens and registers the utf8 library; pushes the library table and returns the number of results (usually 1).
requirements: L must be a valid lua_State*.
Should be called during library initialization or via require-like mechanisms.

functions.name: luaopen_math

functions.name: Luau::Allocator::Allocator
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes an empty page-based bump allocator that hands out uninitialized memory blocks with at least 8-byte alignment. Memory allocated from this allocator is reclaimed only when the allocator is destroyed; individual deallocation is not supported.
requirements: No preconditions on construction.
Allocated memory is managed by this allocator instance and will be released when this object is destroyed; there is no per-allocation free.

Objects placed into memory from this allocator will not have their destructors run by the allocator (per the class’s usage pattern); callers must ensure this is acceptable or handle destruction themselves if they construct non-trivially destructible objects.

functions.name: Luau::Allocator::Allocator
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership of the allocator’s internal pages from another Allocator to this one. After the move, this allocator continues managing the previously allocated memory; the moved-from allocator is left in a valid but unspecified state.
requirements: The source allocator (other) must be an rvalue (temporary or explicitly std::move’d).
After the move, use the moved-from allocator only for destruction or reassignment; do not rely on any of its prior allocations via the moved-from object.
Pointers previously obtained from the source allocator remain valid but are now owned by the moved-to allocator; do not destroy the source expecting it to free those allocations.

functions.name: Luau::Allocator::~Allocator
functions.description: Destructor. Releases all memory pages owned by the allocator in one shot. No destructors are invoked for objects that were constructed in the allocated memory.
requirements: Callers must not dereference or otherwise use any pointers returned by this allocator after it is destroyed.
If non-trivially destructible objects were constructed in allocator memory, the caller is responsible for invoking their destructors before the allocator is destroyed.

functions.name: Luau::Allocator::allocate
functions.description: Allocates an uninitialized contiguous memory block of the requested size from an internal 8 KB page-based bump allocator. The returned pointer is at least 8-byte aligned. Memory is freed only when the allocator is destroyed; there is no per-block free.
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to allocate; behavior for size == 0 is unspecified in this header (caller should avoid zero-sized allocations unless implementation-defined behavior is acceptable).
Returned memory is uninitialized; the caller must initialize it before use.
Alignment is at least 8 bytes based on the allocator’s internal storage; if stronger alignment is required, the caller must provide it manually.
Do not pass the returned pointer to delete/free; memory is owned by the allocator and will be reclaimed only when the allocator is destroyed.
If constructing objects in this memory, note that the allocator will not run destructors; callers must ensure objects are trivially destructible or manually destroy them as needed.

functions.name: Luau::assertHandler

Callers can read the current handler or assign a new one to customize assertion handling. Typical usage: set this to a function matching int(const char* expression, const char* file, int line, const char* function) to control whether a debug break is triggered when LUAU_ASSERT fails.
requirements: When assigning, the target must be a function pointer of type int (*)(const char*, const char*, int, const char*), or nullptr to disable custom handling.

functions.name: Luau::assertCallHandler
functions.signature: LUAU_NOINLINE inline int Luau::assertCallHandler(const char* expression, const char* file, int line, const char* function)
functions.description: Invokes the currently installed Luau assert handler, if any. Returns the handler’s integer result; if no handler is installed, returns 1. Used by LUAU_ASSERT: a nonzero return typically requests a debug break, while zero suppresses it.

If no handler is installed, arguments are ignored; when a handler is installed, passing nullptr for the string parameters may cause handler-defined behavior or crashes.
The function must not rely on side effects in the handler to always occur; when no handler is installed, it returns 1 without invoking anything.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting free-form text bytes suitable for Luau error/message strings
# used by stubs like CompileError, ParseError, Lexer helpers, etc.
# Strategy: build varied-length UTF-8 text with combinations of:
# - ASCII words, punctuation, numbers
# - Lua-like snippets (identifiers, keywords, operators)
# - Quoted and multiline-like chunks
# - Unicode ranges (emoji, CJK, accents)
# - Edge cases: empty, very long (bounded), repeated chars, null bytes inside
# - Newlines and tabs to simulate locations/pretty printers
#
# Max output size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "error", "warning", "info", "debug", "assert", "panic", "exception",
    "line", "column", "position", "token", "lexer", "parser", "bytecode",
    "function", "table", "vector", "userdata", "buffer", "nil", "boolean",
    "number", "string", "thread", "metatable", "coverage", "breakpoint",
]

LUA_KEYWORDS = [
    "and", "break", "do", "else", "elseif", "end", "false", "for", "function",
    "if", "in", "local", "nil", "not", "or", "repeat", "return", "then",
    "true", "until", "while",
]

PUNCT = list(".,;:!?()[]{}<>=+-*/%#|&^~")

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "αβγ", "ΔΣ", "π≈3.14", "žšč", "ñáéíóú", "你好世界", "こんにちは", "안녕하세요",
    "🙂🙃😂", "🧪🔧", "🚀✨", "₀₁₂₃⁴⁵", "¼½¾", "©®™", "€£¥₿",
]

# Some Lua-like snippets that could be helpful in diagnostics
LUA_SNIPPETS = [
    "local x = 42",
    "function f(a, b) return a + b end",
    "if x > 0 then return x else return -x end",
    "for i=1,10 do print(i) end",
    "t = {a=1, [2]=3, ['k']='v'}",
    "--!strict",
    "-- TODO: fix",
    "assert(type(x) == 'number')",
    "error('boom')",
    "print((`hello ${name}`))",
]

# Repeated patterns (including NULs) for edge-case string handling
REPEAT_PATTERNS = [
    "\x00",  # NUL inside string
    "\r\n",
    "\t",
    " ",
    "-",
    "_",
    "=",
]


def _rand_range(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def _rand_ascii_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes random identifier-like
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
        rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 12)))
        return start + rest
    return rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)


def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS)
    # Generate a random BMP character (avoid surrogates)
    cp = rng.randint(0x20, 0xD7FF)
    return chr(cp)


def _rand_punct(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(PUNCT)


def _rand_lua_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(LUA_SNIPPETS)


def _rand_repeat_chunk(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pat = rng.choice(REPEAT_PATTERNS)
    times = _rand_range(rng, 1, 32)
    return pat * times


def _quoted(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    quote = rng.choice(['"', "'"])
    # Occasionally produce an unterminated string to test fixups, but keep valid overall by closing
    body = s.replace(quote, '\\' + quote)
    return f"{quote}{body}{quote}"


def _multiline_block(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Simulate Lua long string/comment with equals
    eqs = '=' * _rand_range(rng, 0, 3)
    return f"[{eqs}[{s}]{eqs}]"


def _make_section(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> str:
    # Build a section up to budget characters with mixed content
    parts: List[str] = []
    while budget > 0 and len(parts) < 50:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.18:
            token = _rand_ascii_word(rng)
        elif choice < 0.30:
            token = rng.choice(LUA_KEYWORDS)
        elif choice < 0.42:
            token = _rand_unicode(rng)
        elif choice < 0.52:
            token = _rand_punct(rng)
        elif choice < 0.62:
            token = _rand_lua_snippet(rng)
        elif choice < 0.72:
            token = _quoted(rng, _rand_ascii_word(rng) + " " + _rand_unicode(rng))
        elif choice < 0.80:
            token = _multiline_block(rng, _rand_lua_snippet(rng))
        elif choice < 0.88:
            token = _rand_repeat_chunk(rng)
        else:
            # Numbers and positions
            token = f"{rng.randint(-999999, 999999)}:{rng.randint(0, 200)}"
        # Separators including newlines/tabs
        sep = rng.choice([" ", " ", "\n", "\t", "\n\n"])  # prefer space but include newlines
        chunk = token + sep
        if len(chunk) > budget:
            chunk = chunk[:budget]
        parts.append(chunk)
        budget -= len(chunk)
    return ''.join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose an overall target size, biased to small-to-medium, sometimes large up to MAX_SIZE
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.15:
        target = rng.randint(0, 32)  # include empty and tiny
    elif mode < 0.85:
        target = rng.randint(64, 1024)
    else:
        target = rng.randint(1025, MAX_SIZE)

    # Compose a header with diagnostic-like prefix occasionally
    header_parts: List[str] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        # file:line:col style
        file_name = _rand_ascii_word(rng) + ".luau"
        header_parts.append(f"{file_name}:{rng.randint(1, 1000)}:{rng.randint(1, 200)}: ")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            header_parts.append(rng.choice(["error: ", "warning: ", "note: "]))
        header_parts.append(_rand_ascii_word(rng))
        header_parts.append("\n")
    header = ''.join(header_parts)

    # Body sections
    remaining = max(0, target - len(header))
    body = _make_section(rng, remaining)

    # Footer with a code excerpt or caret line sometimes
    footer = ""
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(body) < target:
        # Create a simple code line and caret indicator
        code = _rand_lua_snippet(rng)
        caret_pos = rng.randint(1, min(len(code), 60))
        footer = f"\n{code}\n" + (" " * caret_pos) + "^\n"
        # Trim if exceeding target
        over = len(header) + len(body) + len(footer) - target
        if over > 0:
            footer = footer[:-over]

    s = (header + body + footer)[:MAX_SIZE]

    # Ensure UTF-8 encoding; replace errors to keep it valid for C++ std::string usage
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')

    # Occasionally inject a few NUL bytes inside to exercise lua_pushlstring/lua_tolstring paths
    if b and rng.random() < 0.2:
        injects = rng.randint(1, 3)
        ba = bytearray(b)
        for _ in range(injects):
            pos = rng.randint(0, len(ba)-1)
            ba[pos] = 0
        b = bytes(ba)

    # Bound final size
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        b = b[:MAX_SIZE]

    return b

import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator targets arbitrary byte strings used by the fuzz stubs.
# Stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as std::string (binary-safe) and sometimes
# use its pointer/length directly (e.g., StringRef, name tables, compile constants).
# We therefore emit valid, interesting byte sequences that cover:
# - Empty and very short strings
# - Printable ASCII
# - UTF-8 (valid and edge sequences)
# - Binary data with NULs
# - Repeated patterns and varying lengths
# - Long strings up to a safe cap
# The fuzzer framework will reuse the same buffer across multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
# in a single stub invocation; to provide diversity, we package multiple candidate
# strings concatenated with length-prefixed framing so the harness can slice;
# however, typical FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls the whole buffer. To maximize utility,
# we produce a single composite that is still meaningful when taken as a whole:
# it's constructed by concatenating diverse segments to exercise hashing/equality
# and string handling paths while remaining valid byte strings.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_ascii(rng, n):
    # Printable ASCII plus some punctuation
    chars = [c for c in range(32, 127)]
    return bytes(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_utf8_valid(rng, n):
    # Build a valid UTF-8-ish sequence of approx n bytes using codepoints in various ranges
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        kind = rng.randrange(0, 5)
        if kind == 0:
            # ASCII
            out.append(rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F))
        elif kind == 1:
            # 2-byte
            cp = rng.randrange(0x80, 0x7FF)
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        elif kind == 2:
            # 3-byte
            cp = rng.randrange(0x800, 0xFFFF)
            # avoid surrogates
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0xE000
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        elif kind == 3:
            # 4-byte
            cp = rng.randrange(0x10000, 0x10FFFF)
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        else:
            # control/newline/tab
            out.append(rng.choice([0x0A, 0x0D, 0x09, 0x20]))
        if len(out) > n:
            break
    return bytes(out[:n])

def _rand_binary(rng, n):
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pattern_repeat(pattern: bytes, n: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b''
    return (pattern * (n // len(pattern) + 1))[:n]

def _length_prefix(chunks):
    # Prefix each chunk with 4-byte little-endian length for potential consumers
    out = bytearray()
    for c in chunks:
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(c))
        out += c
    return bytes(out)

def _interesting_constants():
    # Common strings that might be used as identifiers, names, or empty
    return [
        b"", b"a", b"A", b"0", b" ", b"\n", b"\x00",
        b"function", b"end", b"local", b"vector", b"_G",
        b"name", b"__index", b"__tostring", b"metatable",
        b"LoremIpsum", b"foo", b"bar", b"baz",
    ]

def _make_segments(rng):
    segs = []

    # 1) Empty
    segs.append(b"")

    # 2) Short ASCII
    segs.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 16)))

    # 3) Valid UTF-8 medium
    segs.append(_rand_utf8_valid(rng, rng.randint(8, 64)))

    # 4) Binary with NULs
    bin_len = rng.randint(8, 64)
    b = bytearray(_rand_binary(rng, bin_len))
    # sprinkle some NULs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, max(1, bin_len // 8))):
        b[rng.randrange(0, bin_len)] = 0
    segs.append(bytes(b))

    # 5) Repeated patterns that stress hashing/equality
    patterns = [b"a", b"\x00", b"abc", b"\xFF\x00", b"Luau", b"name"]
    pat = rng.choice(patterns)
    segs.append(_pattern_repeat(pat, rng.randint(4, 64)))

    # 6) Identifier-like names (likely for AstNameTable)
    ident_len = rng.randint(1, 32)
    first = rng.choice(list(range(ord('A'), ord('Z')+1)) + list(range(ord('a'), ord('z')+1)) + [ord('_')])
    rest_pool = list(range(ord('A'), ord('Z')+1)) + list(range(ord('a'), ord('z')+1)) + list(range(ord('0'), ord('9')+1)) + [ord('_')]
    ident = bytes([first] + [rng.choice(rest_pool) for _ in range(ident_len-1)])
    segs.append(ident)

    # 7) Some constants
    segs.append(rng.choice(_interesting_constants()))

    # 8) Longer UTF-8/binary mix
    long_len = rng.randint(64, 512)
    mix = bytearray()
    while len(mix) < long_len:
        choice = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        if choice == 0:
            mix += _rand_utf8_valid(rng, rng.randint(1, 8))
        elif choice == 1:
            mix += _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 8))
        else:
            mix += _rand_binary(rng, rng.randint(1, 8))
    segs.append(bytes(mix[:long_len]))

    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create multiple segments of varying flavors
    segs = _make_segments(rng)

    # Additionally, duplicate one segment and a slight variant to test equality/inequality
    if segs:
        dup = rng.choice(segs)
        segs.append(dup)  # exact duplicate
        # slight variant (append a byte) while staying valid binary
        segs.append(dup + bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256)]))

    # Pack with length prefixes so consumers that split can use them; consumers that
    # read the whole buffer still get a composite with diverse content.
    data = _length_prefix(segs)

    # Ensure we do not exceed max size
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]
